$comment: Primary block explorer per chain, and how to ask whether a contract's SOURCE is verified.
Keyed exactly as the deployments-v4.json files are, per VM, so joining needs no translation.
'checks' is an ORDERED preference list, not a set. The audit tries each in turn and stops at the
first that says verified, recording WHICH one answered -- a contract verified on any of them is
visible to someone who looks there, so the audit reports where it is actually visible.
etherscan  - PREFERRED. The explorer people actually open, and it recompiles and compares
bytecode itself, so it is the only one of the three that can give us a FULL match.
Needs ETHERSCAN_API_KEY: one V2 key covers 14 of our 16 chains (Tempo is absent
from Etherscan's chain list). Without the key this check reports could-not-check,
never unverified -- a missing key must not manufacture a gap.
sourcify   - Keyless fallback. Ours can only ever reach PARTIAL match: foundry.toml sets
bytecode_hash=none and cbor_metadata=false, and restoring that metadata would
change the initcode and move every CREATE2 address.
blockscout - Keyless fallback, per-chain instances. Present for 11 of 16; Avalanche, Fuji and
Amoy have none. Optimism and OP Sepolia redirect to explorer.optimism.io.
osec       - SVM. Solana has no Etherscan-style source verification; the equivalent is a
verified BUILD in the OtterSec registry. A different guarantee, recorded as such.
[]         - no explorer identified; audited as unresolved, not as absent.

42431.name: Tempo Explorer
42431.note: Tempo has an explorer at https://explore.tempo.xyz (explorer.tempo.xyz redirects there), but no source-verification API responded on it: the Blockscout, Etherscan-compatible and addresses routes all 404, and Tempo is absent from Etherscan's V2 chain list. Recorded as an OPEN QUESTION for Tempo rather than as 'no explorer' -- the explorer exists, the verification path is what is unknown.

5042.name: Arc Explorer
5042.note: Arc's explorer is a Blockscout instance. The testnet API answers api/v2 and already shows the testnet contracts as partially verified; the mainnet host sits behind a Cloudflare challenge that answers plain HTTP clients with 403, so a could-not-check from CI means the challenge, not an unverified contract: open the address page in a browser. Arc is absent from Etherscan's V2 chain list.
